overview: This 483-page file traces Japanese merchant shipping from prewar government controls through wartime shortages and salvage. Consular reports, intelligence, diplomatic correspondence, and legal records document shipbuilding, vessel requisitions and diversions, trade routes, fuel restrictions, and the immunity of government-controlled vessels. It also follows a prolonged Dutch inquiry into cargo discharged from the Sanyo Maru in New York.
interest: Translated requisition orders and monthly reports reveal how Japan tightened shipping control; cargo records show wartime claims in practice.
